chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Said Al-Hamdani, who said: Al-Hasan ibn Al-Qasim recited to me, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Al-Mu'alla narrated to us, who said: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Bakr Al-Muradi narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn, from his father, peace be upon him, who said:

One day, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was sitting with his companions, preparing them for battle, when an old man bearing the signs of travel approached him and asked: 'Where is the Commander of the Faithful?' He was told: 'He is here.' He greeted him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have come to you from the region of Sham. I am an old man who has heard countless virtues about you, and I believe you may be assassinated. Teach me from what Allah has taught you.'

He said: 'Yes, O old man. Whoever's two days are equal is at a loss. Whoever makes this world his main concern will suffer greatly at its departure. Whoever's tomorrow is worse than his today is deprived. Whoever does not care about what he loses from his Hereafter as long as his worldly affairs are intact is destroyed. Whoever does not regularly examine his own shortcomings will be overtaken by his desires. And whoever is in a state of deficiency, death is better for him. O old man, be pleased for people with what you are pleased for yourself and treat people as you would like to be treated.'

Then he turned to his companions and said: 'O people, do you not see how the people of this world end their evenings and begin their mornings in various conditions? Among them is one who is writhing in pain, another visiting and being visited, another struggling with his soul, another who has no hope left, another who is shrouded, one who seeks the world while death is seeking him, one who is heedless yet is not forgotten, and the remaining are following in the footsteps of those who have passed.'

Zayd ibn Suhan Al-Abdi asked him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, which power is the most dominant and strongest?' He replied: 'Desire.' He asked: 'Which humiliation is the most degrading?' He replied: 'Greed for the world.' He asked: 'Which poverty is the most severe?' He replied: 'Disbelief after faith.' He asked: 'Which call is the most misguided?' He replied: 'The one who calls for what cannot be.'

He asked: 'Which deed is the best?' He replied: 'Piety.' He asked: 'Which action is the most successful?' He replied: 'Seeking what is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He asked: 'Who is the worst companion for you?' He replied: 'The one who beautifies disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for you.' He asked: 'Who among creation is the most wretched?' He replied: 'The one who sells his religion for the worldly life of another.'

He asked: 'Who among creation is the strongest?' He replied: 'The one who is patient and forbearing.' He asked: 'Who among creation is the most miserly?' He replied: 'The one who acquires wealth unlawfully and spends it inappropriately.' He asked: 'Who among people is the wisest?' He replied: 'The one who recognizes his guidance from his misguidance and inclines towards his guidance.'

He asked: 'Who among people is the most patient?' He replied: 'The one who does not become angry.' He asked: 'Who among people has the most steadfast opinion?' He replied: 'The one who is not deceived by people about himself and whom the world does not deceive with its attractions.' He asked: 'Who among people is the most foolish?' He replied: 'The one who is deluded by the world despite witnessing its changing conditions.'

He asked: 'Who among people will have the greatest regret?' He replied: 'The one who is deprived of both this world and the Hereafter - that is the clear loss.' He asked: 'Who among creation is the most blind?' He replied: 'The one who acts for other than Allah while seeking reward for his actions from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

He asked: 'Which contentment is the best?' He replied: 'Being content with what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given.' He asked: 'Which affliction is the most severe?' He replied: 'The affliction in religion.' He asked: 'Which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' He replied: 'Awaiting relief (deliverance).'

He asked: 'Who among people is the best in the sight of Allah?' He replied: 'The one who fears Allah the most, acts most righteously with piety, and is the most detached from the world.' He asked: 'Which speech is the best in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' He replied: 'Abundant remembrance of Him and humbly supplicating to Him in prayer.'

He asked: 'Which statement is the most truthful?' He replied: 'The testimony that there is no God but Allah.' He asked: 'Which deeds are the greatest before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' He replied: 'Submission and piety.' He asked: 'Who among people is the most truthful?' He replied: 'The one who is truthful in all circumstances.'

Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, turned to the elderly man and said: 'O old man, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has created people upon whom He has narrowed the worldly life, looking upon them with care. He made them disinterested in it and in its fleeting pleasures, so they longed for the Abode of Peace (Paradise) to which He invited them. They patiently endured the hardship of life and bore difficulties, yearning for the honor that is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

They sacrificed themselves seeking Allah's pleasure, and the conclusion of their deeds was martyrdom. Thus, they met Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while He was pleased with them. They understood that death is the path for those who have passed and those who remain. Therefore, they prepared for their Hereafter, not with gold or silver, but by wearing coarse garments, patiently enduring trials, prioritizing virtue, loving for the sake of Allah, and hating for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
They are the beacons of light and the people of bliss in the Hereafter. And peace be upon you.
The elderly man said: 'Where could I go, leaving Paradise behind when I can see it and see its people with you, O Commander of the Faithful? Equip me with strength so that I may fight your enemies.'

So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, provided him with weapons and provisions. The elderly man joined the battle, fighting in front of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, striking with great vigor. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was amazed at what the elderly man did. When the battle intensified, the elderly man charged his horse forwards until he was martyred - may Allah have mercy on him.

One of the companions of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, followed him and found him lying lifeless, his mount nearby, and his sword still in his hand. When the battle ended, the companion brought his mount and weapons to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him.
The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, prayed over him and said: 'This man, by Allah, is truly fortunate. So seek mercy for your brother.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings of Imam Ali (as) regarding worldly life and the Hereafter in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* presents a dense collection of ethical maxims attributed to Imam Ali (as), emphasizing that true strength lies in self-mastery (*al-Hawa*) and contentment, while the greatest loss is being deprived of both this world and the Hereafter. The narrative arc, where an elderly scholar from Sham is inspired to seek martyrdom after hearing these teachings, illustrates the Shia concept of *Intizar al-Faraj* (waiting for relief) and the spiritual efficacy of concise, profound knowledge (*al-Kalim al-Qasir*). Imam Ali’s declaration of the old man as 'truly fortunate' underscores the Shia valorization of conscious, informed martyrdom over mere physical endurance.
